# People and communication

Good communication makes shared work easier. Agree with your supervisor and collaborators on the channel and response time that fit each kind of question; urgent safety or participant concerns should follow the lab's formal escalation route.

## Who to contact

| Topic | First contact |
|---|---|
| Research direction and priorities | [supervisor / project lead] |
| Equipment or room access | [equipment or facility contact] |
| Participant scheduling | [coordinator / project contact] |
| Data storage and access | [data steward / IT contact] |
| Purchasing and reimbursements | [administrator] |
| Safety, ethics, or adverse events | [official institutional contact and procedure] |

Replace these roles with the lab's agreed contacts and include an approved shared address where possible. Do not put personal phone numbers here without consent.

## Shared work habits

- Put decisions, owners, and deadlines in a place collaborators can find.
- Tell collaborators when a plan or timeline changes.
- Ask early when you are blocked or unsure about a procedure.
- Respect confidentiality and use approved channels for sensitive information.
